skill.name: frontend-dev-guidelines
skill.description: Frontend development guidelines for Next.js 15 apps using React 19, TypeScript, Shadcn/ui, and Tailwind CSS. It covers components, routing, data fetching, file structure, styling, and performance.
skill.summary: Apply consistent Next.js 15 frontend patterns for components, routing, data fetching, styling, and TypeScript.
skill.author: 0Chan-smc

security_audit.summary: The alerts are false positives from Markdown backticks, TypeScript examples, JSX tokens, and one example.com fetch snippet in SKILL.md. I found no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, executable scripts, or hidden runtime behavior in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: - [ ] Add `"use client"` directive only if needed (interactivity, hooks, browser APIs)
- **Server Components** (default): No `"use client"`, can fetch data directly, smaller bundle
- **Client Components**: Add `"use client"` for interactivity, hooks, browser APIs
- No need for `useEffect` or data fetching libraries
- Customize via `className` prop or CSS variables
2. **App Router Structure**: Use file-based routing with `app/` directory
8. **Import Aliases**: Use `@/` prefix for clean imports

content.user_title: Build Next.js Frontends with Clear Patterns
content.value_statement: Next.js teams need consistent patterns for components, routing, data fetching, and styling. This skill provides practical guidance for React 19, App Router, Shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, and TypeScript.
actual_capabilities: Choose Server Components or Client Components for common frontend tasks.
Outline App Router pages, loading states, error boundaries, and dynamic routes.
Apply Shadcn/ui imports, Tailwind CSS classes, and the cn utility.
Describe data fetching with Server Components and mutations with Server Actions.
Provide TypeScript patterns for props, imports, forms, and reusable components.
limitations: It is guidance only and does not inspect or modify files by itself.
Examples use placeholder APIs and must be adapted for real services.
It focuses on Next.js 15, not older Pages Router projects.
It does not replace accessibility, security, or performance testing.

use_cases.title: Create Feature Pages
use_cases.description: Frontend developers can structure new App Router pages with related components, loading states, and metadata.

use_cases.title: Standardize Component Work
use_cases.description: Engineering leads can align teams around Server Components, Client Components, Shadcn/ui imports, and TypeScript props.

use_cases.title: Review Frontend Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Code reviewers can check routing, styling, data fetching, and performance choices against a shared checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Next.js 15 component plan for a profile card. Include whether it should be a Server Component or Client Component.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an App Router page for a product list. Include file placement, loading state, error boundary, metadata, and data fetching approach.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this frontend feature for Next.js 15 patterns. Suggest changes for component boundaries, imports, Tailwind usage, and TypeScript types.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Frontend Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate a multi-page dashboard flow. Check App Router structure, Server Actions, Suspense usage, form validation, and performance tradeoffs.

output_examples.input: Request: Build a posts list page with server-side data fetching.
output_examples.output: A structured page plan that names the route file, uses a Server Component, adds loading and error states, and calls out metadata.

output_examples.input: Request: Convert an interactive form to a Next.js 15 pattern.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to use a Client Component for form state, Server Actions for submission, and zod validation.

output_examples.input: Request: Review a component library import plan.
output_examples.output: A checklist covering Shadcn/ui import paths, shared component placement, Tailwind class composition, and TypeScript prop definitions.

best_practices: Default to Server Components and add client directives only for browser APIs or hooks.
Keep route files, feature components, actions, and types in predictable App Router locations.
Use strict TypeScript, Shadcn/ui components, Tailwind utilities, and explicit loading and error states.
anti_patterns: Adding client directives to every component without a browser-side requirement.
Mixing reusable UI components with feature-specific route code.
Using placeholder API URLs, loose types, or missing validation in production code.

faq.question: Does this skill run commands?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown guideline skill and does not execute shell commands by itself.

faq.question: Which frameworks does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Next.js 15 with React 19, TypeScript, Shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, and App Router.

faq.question: Can it help with existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it to review component boundaries, route structure, styling, data fetching, and TypeScript patterns.

faq.question: Does it support Pages Router?
faq.answer: Only indirectly. The guidance focuses on App Router patterns and may not fit Pages Router projects.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It provides patterns and examples. Teams must adapt placeholders, test behavior, and review security requirements.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The metadata marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
